candidates.title: OpenAI puts four GPT-4 API families on a 90-day migration clock
candidates.summary: OpenAI notified API developers that specific GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1 mini snapshots—and fine-tunes based on them—will shut down on January 14, 2027.
candidates.what_changed: Five pinned snapshot IDs across four GPT-4 families now have a single January 14, 2027 shutdown date and `gpt-6-luna` as the recommended replacement; affected fine-tuned versions follow the same schedule.
candidates.why_it_matters: Production systems may have prompts, schemas, tool behavior, quality thresholds, and fine-tunes calibrated to these snapshots. A replacement recommendation does not establish behavioral parity, so the notice creates a time-bounded evaluation and rollout program.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Inventory pinned IDs and fine-tuned descendants, replay production-representative evals against the exact replacement configuration, measure quality/latency/token cost, and complete a staged cutover before January 14.

evidence.rationale: OpenAI's canonical API deprecation page names every affected snapshot, the shutdown date, the recommended replacement, and the fine-tune scope.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent replacement-parity testing was found or performed during this run.
evidence.claim_scope: The story treats the lifecycle notice as established and presents migration testing as editorial guidance; it makes no claim that the recommended replacement is behaviorally equivalent.

signal.rationale: A 90-day shutdown window for widely deployed API snapshots and their fine-tunes directly affects production reliability, evaluation work, and change-management schedules.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: Pulse has covered individual model deprecations, but not a reusable migration method for pinned snapshots and fine-tuned descendants.
learning_gap.suggested_explainer: How to Migrate a Pinned Model Without Losing Its Behavioral Contract

follow_up_opportunities.reason: The deadline exposes a reusable workflow for dependency inventory, representative replay, fine-tune migration, canary routing, and rollback.

deduplication.canonical_event: OpenAI announces January 14, 2027 API shutdown for listed GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 snapshots and their fine-tunes.
deduplication.material_delta: No merged Pulse story or ledger covers this October 14 GPT-4-series notice, its affected snapshot list, its January deadline, or its fine-tune scope.

publication_verification.notes: The canonical deprecation page was rechecked on October 15. Replacement parity and migration effort are not claimed as verified.

candidates.title: HydraFusion now spends more reasoning on review than drafting
candidates.summary: GitHub updated HydraFusion with stage-specific reasoning effort, conditional judging and repair, workspace-grounded parallel critics, a refreshed model pool, and a higher-effort Max option.
candidates.what_changed: HydraFusion now uses medium reasoning effort for initial drafts and high effort for review; Cascade can judge and repair only when needed; Critique uses tools to inspect the workspace and parallel critic models; Max applies higher effort to demanding tasks.
candidates.why_it_matters: The release makes model effort, workspace inspection, judgment, and repair independently schedulable parts of a coding-agent workflow rather than properties of one session-wide model choice.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: Evaluate agentic coding systems by stage: define what critics must inspect, measure false accepts and unnecessary repairs, track cost and latency per stage, and keep deterministic tests authoritative when model reviewers disagree.

evidence.rationale: GitHub's dated changelog documents the stage-specific effort, Cascade and Critique changes, model pool, Max option, clients, plan access, and continued research-preview status.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent benchmark of the October HydraFusion changes was available during this run.
evidence.claim_scope: The story describes GitHub's documented orchestration behavior and derives evaluation questions; it does not claim a measured quality, latency, or token advantage.

signal.rationale: Stage-aware reasoning and workspace-grounded review are durable design choices for coding-agent quality and cost control, not a cosmetic client update.

learning_gap.existing_explainer_status: The material update can teach the architecture directly while linking the September HydraFusion story.

follow_up_opportunities.reason: Independent task-level traces or benchmark data would support a separate analysis of judge false-accept rates, critic diversity, stage cost, and repair efficiency.

deduplication.canonical_event: GitHub updates HydraFusion orchestration and introduces HydraFusion Max on October 14, 2026.
deduplication.material_delta: The September story covered initial multi-model planning, drafting, critique, revision, and escalation. The October release adds explicit per-stage effort, a conditional judge/repair step, tool-grounded parallel critics, a new model pool, cross-client availability details, and a distinct Max operating mode.

publication_verification.notes: The October changelog and September canonical story were rechecked. Product behavior remains vendor-documented and benchmark-free.

watchlist.title: ToFu fuzzes semantic trust failures across MCP tools
watchlist.summary: A preprint proposes metadata-derived semantic checks and fuzzing harnesses for the LLM-orchestrator-tool boundary across 273 MCP servers and 3,405 tools.
watchlist.what_changed: The paper reports a large empirical scan of tool implementations, but the arXiv abstract says bugs were found in 343 tools while the comments say there were 253 verified semantic security bugs.

evidence.rationale: The 33-page preprint exposes methods and appendices, but its public metadata contains a material inconsistency in the headline verified-bug count.

signal.rationale: Semantic validation at the tool boundary is a central agent-security problem, and the claimed corpus is unusually broad.

watchlist.reason: A central result is internally inconsistent between the arXiv abstract and comments, so publication would require choosing or obscuring a disputed metric.
promote_when: authors correct or reconcile the 343-tool versus 253-bug count
public artifacts permit replication of the corpus and semantic oracles

watchlist.title: First-price auctions for prompt-routing markets
watchlist.summary: A new theory preprint studies strategic first-price auctions in which AI agents bid for prompts based on expected reward minus inference cost.
watchlist.what_changed: The authors derive welfare bounds under competitive-floor and near-independence assumptions and simulate strategic bidders on the EmbedLLM routing dataset.

evidence.rationale: The result is a new preprint with theoretical guarantees and simulated strategic bidding, not evidence from a deployed agent market.

signal.rationale: The mechanism could inform future decentralized model routing, but today's engineering consequence is speculative.

watchlist.reason: Interesting mechanism-design work, but the validation uses simulated bidders rather than an operating routing market.
promote_when: implementation details from a deployed agent-routing market

exclusions.reason: The October 14 retirement executed a September 11 notice; the cutoff adds no new capability, implementation detail, or migration guidance beyond the previously announced event.
Useful software-supply-chain functionality, but the change has no specific AI engineering consequence and would require artificial scope expansion.
Institutional partnership news without a concrete technical release, engineering configuration, deployment result, or independently evaluable implementation detail.
